title: Unique integer degree on a projective-bundle fibre
statement: Let S be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], E a quasi-coherent finite locally free module of constant rank r >= 2 [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module], and D a normalized tautological quotient on p:P(E)->S [lem-trf-projective-bundle-quotient-geometry]. Let L be an invertible module on P(E) [def-sc-invertible-module], and s a point of S. On the scheme-theoretic fibre i_s:P(E)_s->P(E) [def-pc-scheme-fibre], there is a unique integer m for which i_s^*L is isomorphic to i_s^*(integerLinePower D.line D.invertible m), using [def-pc-module-pullback] and [def-sfb-locally-constant-line-twist]. This asserts nothing about any neighbourhood of s.

source.place: Tag 0BXJ, lemma-Pic-projective-space-UFD, applied over each residue field; EGA II Remark 4.2.7, field calculation.

proof.text: Apply the standard fibre-and-line model to obtain e:P^(r-1)_kappa(s) isomorphic to p.fiber(s), with e^* i_s^* D.line isomorphic to O(1).

source.place: Tags 01OA and 01OE, section-projective-bundle and example-projective-space; lemma-relative-proj-base-change, Tag 01O3.

proof.text: Pull L to standard projective space; invertibility is preserved by tensor pullback, using uniqueness of its adjunction with ordinary module pullback. When r=2 apply the existing projective-line classification. When r>=3 the ring of each chart is a polynomial ring over a field, hence a UFD with trivial Picard group. The affine invertible-sections theorem therefore gives an actual free generator g_i on each chart. The unit relating g_i and g_j satisfies the cocycle equation by injectivity of multiplication by a free generator on every subopen. Normalize this function cocycle, rescale the generators by its chart units, and glue the frame-preserving isomorphisms to O(d).

source.place: Tag 0BXJ, lemma-Pic-projective-space-UFD, double- and triple-overlap calculation.

proof.text: For the composite g=e.hom;i_s, tensor pullback preserves the unit and tensor products. Given g^*D.line isomorphic to O(1), use tensor cancellation by O(1) and the pulled-back dual evaluation to identify g^*(dual D.line) with O(-1). Induction on natural powers gives g^* integerLinePower(D.line,m) isomorphic to O(m), for both signs of m. Pullback composition identifies this with e^* i_s^* integerLinePower(D.line,m).

source.place: Tag 0BXJ, lemma-Pic-projective-space-UFD, double- and triple-overlap calculation.

proof.text: If O(a) is isomorphic to O(b), tensor with O(-a) to identify O(0) with O(b-a). If b<a then H^0(O(b-a))=0, whereas H^0(O(0)) is the degree-zero polynomial submodule and contains the distinct elements 0 and 1. Thus a<=b. Apply the same argument to the inverse isomorphism to obtain b<=a, proving a=b.

source.place: Tag 0BXJ, lemma-Pic-projective-space-UFD, double- and triple-overlap calculation.

proof.text: Compose the isomorphism for the pulled-back L with the inverse power comparison, and pull back along e.inv. The identity and composition isomorphisms recover an isomorphism on the original fibre. Any second integer pulls back to a second standard twist of L; composing the two isomorphisms and applying the preceding separation argument forces equality.

lean.statement:
theorem projective_bundle_fiber_degree (S : Scheme.{u}) (E : S.Modules)
    [E.IsQuasicoherent] (r : ℕ)
    [SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u} E r] (hr : 2 ≤ r)
    (D : TautologicalQuotient E)
    (L : (SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.gradedAlgebraData E).relProj.Modules)
    (hL : L.IsInvertible) (s : S) :
    ∃! m : ℤ, Nonempty
      ((tensorPullback
        ((SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.gradedAlgebraData E).relProjHom.fiberι s)).obj L ≅
        (tensorPullback
          ((SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.gradedAlgebraData E).relProjHom.fiberι s)).obj
          (integerLinePower D.line D.invertible m))
